prompt:
Generate a high-resolution flat UI design presentation board with FOUR complete mobile screens side by side for Custra. These are the next screens of the SAME minimal pastel app shown in the reference image. Closely inherit the reference's layout language, muted sage buttons with DARK labels, warm ivory background, navy/slate text, mist-blue accents, thin neutral rules, folded-C sage/teal logo, gentle line icons and quiet typography. Four equally sized 390x844 equivalent screen frames, readable UI text, small external captions "Product details", "Register complaint", "Choose date", "Choose time". No perspective phone hardware, no giant decorative banners, no unnecessary cards nested in cards. This is a static conceptual UI board with fictional sample content, not actual booking evidence.

SCREEN 1 PRODUCT DETAILS: compact top bar with back arrow, small Custra folded-C emblem and title 'Product details', small 'Edit' link right. A modest flat television category icon, nickname 'Living room TV', secondary 'Samsung · Television'. A quiet sage status pill 'Under warranty' with small note 'Based on your saved details'. Compact primary row/button 'View ongoing complaint', and secondary text action '+ Report another issue'. Below a clean active-complaint strip separated by neutral lines: 'Current complaint', 'Screen won’t turn on', '#DEMO-1042 · Choose appointment', action 'Choose time →'. Product detail rows 'Purchase date' / '20 Oct 2025', 'Warranty period' / '24 months', 'Warranty until' / '20 Oct 2027'. Section 'Documents' with small file icon row 'Purchase invoice.pdf', 'View' at right, subtle '+ Add document'. Near bottom collapsed row 'Past complaints' with chevron. Bottom navigation Home Products Appointments, Products active. Keep compact and minimal, no giant product illustration, no verified contract badges or made-up serial numbers.

SCREEN 2 REGISTER COMPLAINT: back arrow and small logo, title 'Register complaint'. Compact product selector summary shows fridge icon, 'Kitchen fridge', 'Samsung · Refrigerator' and 'Change'. This screen intentionally uses a different saved product from Product Details so it is a distinct fictional example, not a duplicate of the existing TV complaint. One clear required large text field labeled 'What’s wrong?' with fictional entered text 'The fridge is not cooling properly.' and short example/helper 'A short description is enough.' Next 'Service address' with compact unboxed summary 'Home', '12 Sample Lane, Pune · 411001', and 'Change' link. Next 'Contact details' with 'Demo Customer', 'demo@example.test', 'Phone saved' and 'Edit' link, no real personal data. One concise muted note 'Custra will answer using these details.' Large sage primary button 'Register complaint' anchored above bottom navigation. Quiet small 'Business support is simulated.' No separate Issue summary field, no repeated description, no date/time selection here, no chatbot composer, no document requirement. Navigation Home Products Appointments, Home active.

SCREEN 3 CHOOSE DATE: a full-height appointment-selection mobile sheet, only one compact top bar with back arrow, title 'Choose a date' and Close X. Small line 'Living room TV · #DEMO-1042', small quiet 'Demo availability · IST'. Step text '1 of 2 · Date'. A familiar clean accessible MONTH CALENDAR 'October 2026', month arrows visually consistent. Sunday-first weekday labels Sun Mon Tue Wed Thu Fri Sat. Accurate October 2026 geometry: first row blanks Sunday through Wednesday then 1 Thu, 2 Fri, 3 Sat; following rows 4-10, 11-17, 18-24, 25-31. Today in this fictional demo is 17 October. Dates before offered schedule are disabled. Offered dates 19,20,22,23 have availability, 21 explicitly unavailable. Selected 20 marked by muted sage filled circle and dark readable number. Grey other dates with limited contrast while maintain legibility, not selectable-looking. Small legend 'Available' as tiny sage dot and 'No slots' grey dash, never color only. Below calendar selected-date summary 'Tuesday, 20 October' and 'Choose a time next'. Full-width sage button 'Choose time →' near bottom. Small 'Dates reflect the simulated service schedule.' The date sheet overlays normal navigation so do not show bottom tabs inside this task sheet; bottom safe area clear. Do not show stacked dialogs or lots of chips.

SCREEN 4 CHOOSE TIME: matching full-height sheet with back arrow, title 'Choose a time', Close X. Small context 'Living room TV · #DEMO-1042'. Step text '2 of 2 · Time'. Clear selected date 'Tue, 20 October 2026' with visible 'Change date' link adjacent; always allow going back. 'All times IST · Demo availability'. SIX compact selectable time tiles in TWO columns and THREE rows, with realistic one-hour ranges and explicit unavailable labels: '9–10 AM' available, '10–11 AM' disabled with 'Unavailable'; '11 AM–12 PM' SELECTED sage background with dark text and checkmark, '12–1 PM' available; '2–3 PM' disabled with 'Unavailable', '3–4 PM' available. Grey unavailable text remains readable, no click affordance for unavailable slots. Near bottom simple unboxed confirmation summary 'Tue, 20 Oct · 11 AM–12 PM IST', 'Home · Pune'. Full-width sage button 'Confirm appointment'. Secondary 'Choose a different date' text link may be omitted because Change date is already clear near top. Below button quiet 'Simulated appointment'. No bottom navigation inside the sheet, no fake confirmed booking before user confirms.

The overall board must be extremely consistent with the reference and should prove the end-to-end low-effort flow, not introduce a different aesthetic. Preserve warm minimal utility. Avoid saturated royal blue, strong gradients on controls, marketing slogans, unnecessary explanatory banners, tiny unreadable text, inconsistent icon styles or oversize headings. Make all four complete screens fully visible.
notes: Four states covering three core areas: product detail, complaint intake, calendar, times/confirmation.
Fictional content and simulated availability; no actual booking or application implementation.

Implementation must keep unavailable date numerals visible (the generated calendar shows a dash at 21), retain dark readable date/slot labels, and avoid verified-entitlement implications from warranty icon.
Warranty expiry arithmetic and boundary conventions remain to be specified; example dates are illustrative.
